Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 27, 2026, 8:28 AM ET / 12:28 UTC (Revision 63)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch replaces separate SQLite state and device-identity coordinators with native transactions and state-local process ownership, revises worker and temporary-artifact cleanup, and fixes a stale Wear audio frame. > [!WARNING] > **SQLite table change** > > This PR modifies persisted SQLite tables in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/DeviceIdentitySQLiteStore.swift`. Prefer a design that avoids changing persisted SQLite tables. If the change is necessary, verify migration and upgrade compatibility against an existing database before merge. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 6 items remain** Keep open. Current main and the latest release still use separate SQLite coordination, while this PR has substantial real-boundary proof for the replacement. The conflict-resolved head still lacks observed installed-updater automatic restart, an upgrade path identified in the prior review. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `cf7b08c7a82c56f766c2d01b7a805422f5a7d4d8` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The branch has strong real-boundary evidence and no confirmed patch defect, with one material final-head upgrade observation still unresolved. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (terminal): Real SQLite/filesystem controls exercise the introduced state owner with a foreign writer and show refusal before its write; published-updater runs on earlier candidates show state survival and rollback, and inspected images show the Wear frame result. The final-head automatic restart gap remains an independent upgrade risk. The canonical state schema version and staging-token format are unchanged, so no stored-data migration contract was introduced. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (terminal): Real SQLite/filesystem controls exercise the introduced state owner with a foreign writer and show refusal before its write; published-updater runs on earlier candidates show state survival and rollback, and inspected images show the Wear frame result. The final-head automatic restart gap remains an independent upgrade risk. The canonical state schema version and staging-token format are unchanged, so no stored-data migration contract was introduced. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Current-main boundary: Current main still imports and acquires the separate lifecycle coordinator; the central cutover remains unique to this PR.

### Wear avatar: stale audio frame before and after

A controlled synthetic replay blocks an old audio frame immediately after dequeue, replaces PCM playback, and then releases the canceled old job. Before the fix, the stale frame changes the real mouth-level state from `0.27854604` to `1.0`. With the PR implementation, the old job reaches the same point and its identity guard preserves `0.27854604`.

Both images use the unchanged production `WearTalkAvatar` through Compose/Robolectric's native Skia renderer: speaking state, dark production colors, identical PCM and frame settings, animation scale 1, and 61 frame timestamps ending at one second. These are synthetic native-renderer captures. Temporary scheduling instrumentation existed only in the disposable proof copy and has been removed. The two final proof runs took 44.60 seconds including incremental builds.

Validation update for `41022bf71e56fc2d98f69a21cb0320a5898ee373`:

The original [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36121653444) passed the device-publication regression shard, then timed out in `models-connect-publication.integration.test.ts`. The recorded phases stop during Gateway startup/connect, before any catalog assertion: state setup at 0 ms, startup/connect entered at 326 ms, timeout at 60,048 ms, zero snapshots and zero active root work. The test, helper and port-claim sources are unchanged from current main. The stop-after-failure policy cancelled the remaining jobs; these were not provisioning failures.

A replay of the exact 16-file constituent, its two configurations, include order and eight workers passed all 190 tests locally in 179.90 s; the affected case took 20.00 s. That macOS replay does not establish the Linux cause. A separate Linux reproduction was stopped by its resource preflight because the allocated machine had four CPUs and about 15.4 GiB, below the constituent's 28 GiB requirement. No tests ran on that machine, and its lease is being released.

No safe owning defect has been established for this timeout. The original failure remains recorded. The next step is one hosted rerun of failed/cancelled checks on this unchanged commit, with the workflow's normal runner policy. Assertions, timeouts, test selection and source remain unchanged. A passing replay will not be described as a timeout fix. Exact-head published-updater acceptance is also still required before merge.
